era_setting.notes: The night is 26 March 2024. The film runs forward to the NTSB board meeting of 18 November 2025 and the indictment unsealed 12 May 2026, so 2020s American and Singaporean maritime settings are correct throughout. No opening date for the bridge is sourced in the ledger (KB-118), so no year for its construction may appear as fact.

forbidden_claims: That Synergy Marine, Synergy Maritime or Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair caused the collapse. They are charged, not convicted (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-501).
That anyone lied to the NTSB. The charge is false statements and obstruction of an agency proceeding; a charge is not a finding (FACTS_LEDGER rows KB-402, KB-409, KB-501).
That the ship would have cleared the bridge with the proper fuel pumps. The indictment alleges it (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-408).
That the civil settlement was an admission of liability or of any fact (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-305).
That the Maryland Transportation Authority knew the bridge was vulnerable. The Board found they were likely unaware (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-205).
Any length in feet for the Dali stated as fact. Three official documents give 947, 984 and 900 (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-601).
That all four blackouts happened before the ship sailed. Two were in port on 25 March, two were under way on 26 March (FACTS_LEDGER rows KB-101 to KB-113).
That the complete NTSB report has been published, unless that has been checked first (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-207).
Any cause of death, injury detail, or identification of the six men beyond what an official record states.

That Nair directed the chief engineer to send a concealing email, stated as fact. That is the chief engineer's account of a charged defendant who has not been tried, and it must be attributed to him and paired with the presumption of innocence (FACTS_LEDGER rows KB-709, KB-501).

That the chief engineer's admissions are findings against anyone else. He admitted his own failure to report a hazardous condition; the three indicted defendants are unaffected by it (FACTS_LEDGER rows KB-704, KB-501).

That the flushing pump caused the collapse. The NTSB's probable cause is the loose wire and the label banding; the pump is the indictment's separate allegation about why the ship did not recover (FACTS_LEDGER row KB-603).

beats.notes: The timestamp the duty officer gave the order. Held silent, no music.

beats.headline: SIXTY-SEVEN SECONDS
beats.notes: Arithmetic on two sourced timestamps, not an estimate. 01:27:53 to about 01:29.

beats.headline: THREE SHIP LENGTHS OUT
beats.notes: 0.6 miles. Do NOT convert to feet -- three official documents disagree on the ship's length (KB-601).

beats.headline: IN PORT / UNDER WAY
beats.notes: Two blackouts on each side of the departure. This card exists to stop the four-in-port error.

beats.headline: THE SWITCH THEY MADE IN PORT
beats.notes: HR2/LR2/TR2, used for months, replaced by HR1/LR1/TR1 -- the configuration the ship sailed on.

beats.headline: HOW A SHIP IS MEANT TO RESTART
A BAND OF LABEL, ON ONE WIRE
beats.notes: The Board's mechanism: the banding stopped the wire seating in the spring-clamp gate. Illustrate the part, never a readable document.

beats.headline: WHAT THE INDICTMENT CHARGES
beats.notes: Four counts, built one line at a time. The card must carry the word CHARGES, never a verdict.

beats.headline: WHAT THEY OFFERED / WHAT WAS CLAIMED
SIXTY-EIGHT BRIDGES
beats.notes: The number the NTSB told the country to go and look at.

beats.headline: MERELY AN ACCUSATION
beats.notes: The Department of Justice's own sentence, on screen, in full. This is the R3 safeguard made visible.

notes: EP77 is the first episode on the rebuilt road and the first bound by ae_beats (decisions/0011). Runtime band 1740-1920s is an owner decision of 2026-08-23, taken from the measured retention profile: 25-43 minute episodes hold 16.0 median minutes against 1.9 for 10-15 minute episodes (funnel snapshot 2026-08-01..07, n=4 long, so the direction is established and the magnitude is not). Word band is that runtime at the measured 160 wpm, never 176. The subject is a LIVE criminal case: the indictment was unsealed 12 May 2026 and forbidden_claims is generated from the ledger's section G. AE beat sources are written as 'FACTS_LEDGER row KB-xxx' rather than the bare id because the schema requires eight characters and a bare id is six -- an owner decision of 2026-08-23 to fix it in the writing rather than by loosening the schema.
